title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
layout_note: Three panels (a), (b), (c) separated by dashed vertical rules: (a) the two mappings between the domains; (b) the forward cycle and its loss; (c) the backward cycle and its loss, mirroring (b).
grouping: Panels are separated by dashed vertical rules and labelled (a), (b), (c) below; (b) and (c) have the same structure.
shapes_depth: Plain black squares for the domains, curved arrows for the mappings, coloured dots for samples; serif math labels.
proposed_highlight: No highlight; each loss gets its own panel.
lesson: Give each loss its own panel of the same structure, so the reader compares the panels instead of untangling one diagram.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue ICCV 2017 (not verified in this session). Card written while studying arrangement (2026-11-15).

arrangement.units: three panels side by side behind dashed vertical rules; (b) and (c) are mirror images
arrangement.inputs_as: a domain square or sample at the left of each panel
arrangement.losses_at: each cycle-consistency loss inside its own panel, labelled with a dotted leader
arrangement.shared: the mappings G and F are redrawn in each panel

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: the two domains X and Y face each other with the mappings G (arc over the top) and F (arc underneath) between them, and each cycle panel ends with the original and reconstructed sample paired by a cycle-consistency brace

relations.form: domain squares X and Y side by side in panel (a), linked by a top arc G and a bottom arc F; in (b)/(c) a brace joins the starting dot and its reconstruction inside one domain square
in (b) and (c) a top row x -> Y_hat -> x_hat (and y -> X_hat -> y_hat) runs left to right with curved arrows labelled G and F
three panels separated by dashed vertical rules, (b) forward cycle and (c) backward cycle drawn as mirror images of the same layout
below each cycle row, two domain squares hold coloured sample dots and the round trip is drawn as arcs between the dots

channels.colour: blue dot = a sample from X, red dot = a sample from Y (in panel (b) and (c)); otherwise monochrome, so G and F are told apart only by label
channels.shape: square = a domain or a sample of a domain; dot = an individual sample inside a domain square
channels.line: solid curved arrow = a mapping (G or F); dotted up-arrow = a discriminator reading a domain; thick dotted leader = points from the brace to the cycle-consistency loss label
channels.frame: none beyond the domain squares; panels are split by thin dashed rules

quality.strengths: Position carries the method: the two domains face each other with the two mappings as opposite arcs, and the cycle loss is drawn as a brace between the original dot and its reconstruction, so what is compared is visible as geometry; (b) and (c) are exact mirrors.
quality.weaknesses: No real images, so the domain abstraction must be known in advance; the brace in (b) is on X's left while in (c) it is on Y's right, which suits the mirror but separates the two loss labels to the outer edges; G and F share one line style and colour.

insights.structure: Three panels (a), (b), (c) separated by dashed vertical rules: (a) domains X and Y linked by mappings G and F with discriminators above; (b) forward cycle x -> Y_hat -> x_hat; (c) backward cycle mirroring (b).
insights.data: Domains are large squares with italic math letters; samples are blue and red dots inside domain squares; discriminators D_X, D_Y sit above with dotted up-arrows.
insights.emphasis: The cycle-consistency loss is a brace between the original and reconstructed dot with a dotted leader to the label, inside each cycle panel.
insights.flow: Left to right; curved arrows for mappings (G over the top, F underneath) and curved arcs between dots in the domain squares.
insights.avoid: Purely abstract: no example images, so the reader must already know what domains mean; monochrome styling gives no colour distinction between G and F.
